title: Centre of gravity and one-force moments practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, wording, values and planned diagrams are original; mapped official evidence informs demand only.

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: controlled definitions to integrated centre-of-gravity and angled one-force moment
question_set_contract.dependency_exception: This is the first lesson and module in the topic pathway. No previous lesson or module exists, so no dependency pair is fabricated; declared Topic 1 and Topic 3 knowledge is used only as prerequisite support.

questions.prompt: State the meaning of (a) centre of gravity and (b) the moment of a force about a point.
A non-uniform object has weight distributed through its material. Which single-force model is used when analysing its turning effect?

options.A: The whole weight acts at the geometric centre in every object.
options.B: The whole weight acts vertically downward through the centre of gravity.
options.C: The whole weight acts at the nearest support point.
options.D: The whole weight acts horizontally through the centre of gravity.

questions.prompt: A force of 18 N has a line of action 0.40 m from a pivot. The stated distance is perpendicular to the line of action. What is the magnitude of the moment about the pivot?
A force is applied at the far end of a rigid handle, but its line of action passes through the pivot. What is its moment about the pivot?

options.A: Zero, because the perpendicular distance is zero.
options.B: Force multiplied by the full handle length.
options.C: Force divided by the full handle length.
options.D: It cannot be found unless the object's mass is known.

questions.prompt: A technician pushes vertically downward with a force of 32 N on the right side of a horizontal handle. The perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force's line of action is 0.28 m. Calculate the moment about the pivot and state whether it is clockwise or anticlockwise.

A non-uniform display arm of mass 3.6 kg extends horizontally to the right of a pivot. Its centre of gravity is 0.42 m from the pivot. Using g = 9.81 N kg^-1, represent the arm's distributed weight by one force and calculate the magnitude and sense of the moment of this weight about the pivot.

figure.purpose: Assess placement of the equivalent weight force and a direct moment calculation
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a non-uniform horizontal display arm pivoted at the left. Mark the centre of gravity 0.42 m from the pivot but omit the weight arrow and turning-direction arrow so the learner must supply them in the response.
figure.alt_text: A non-uniform horizontal display arm has a pivot at the left and its centre of gravity marked 0.42 m away.

questions.prompt: A solar panel of mass 8.0 kg is hinged at its left end and extends upward to the right. Its centre of gravity is 0.75 m from the hinge along the panel. The panel is 40 degrees above the horizontal. Using g = 9.81 N kg^-1, calculate the magnitude and sense of the moment of the panel's weight about the hinge. Then state the moment when the panel is vertical with its centre of gravity directly above the hinge.

figure.purpose: Assess selection of the perpendicular distance for vertical weight on an angled object
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white diagram of a solar panel hinged at the left and tilted 40 degrees above a horizontal guide. Mark the centre of gravity 0.75 m along the panel. Do not draw the weight arrow, perpendicular distance, moment direction or calculation.
figure.alt_text: A solar panel is hinged at one end, tilted 40 degrees above horizontal, with its centre of gravity 0.75 m along the panel.
